title: Fats Waller's radio show and the Ink Spots in Cincinnati
summary: Fats Waller had the Rhythm Club show on WLW, replaced by the Ink Spots, whose member Hoppy got his name there.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: Was Fats staying in that part of the country?

Yeah, he was staying in Cincinnati at the time. He had a show at WLW called "The Rhythm Club," which was taken from the Rhythm Club up here in Harlem -- I mean, it was named after that, you understand. And he had kind of an act on the air.

That's the first time the Ink Spots got to be known. Because Fats had a little disagreement, I think, with his management at WLW, so they hired the Ink Spots to take their place. And they had a guy in there called Hoppy in that show. And Hoppy... It was Hoppy... That was the guy's name that was with the Ink Spots. That's how he got the name Hoppy, because he was, you know...he had that character. And they had kept calling him Hoppy when they got to be the Ink Spots. Do you understand?
They were from Indianapolis, I think. Yeah, most of them...
